---
title: "Pre-push checks"
description: "Run the build-free changed-files gate before pushing so cheap CI failures are caught locally in seconds."
updatedAt: "2026-10-23"
---

## Why this gate exists

Most avoidable CI failures come from cheap checks skipped before pushing: Biome
formatting, `flutter analyze` infos (fatal in CI), TypeScript errors such as
`TS6059` (a package importing app source outside its `rootDir`), stale generated
inventories and branch names the checker rejects. `bun check` is too heavy for
agent machines because its Turbo graph can build workspace dependencies, so it
is not run locally. `bun check:changed` is the replacement before every push.

```bash
bun check:changed                 # working tree vs merge base with origin/main
bun check:changed --dry-run       # print the planned steps only
bun check:changed --only biome    # one step (ids or prefixes such as type-check)
bun check:changed --skip vitest   # skip a step family
bun check:changed --committed     # committed changes only (the hook's mode)
bun check:changed --files a.ts b.ts
```

It never runs builds, `bun check` or Turbo. Small repository scripts run directly;
Vitest, type-check and `flutter analyze` are queued through `ttr resources run`
when resource control is installed and enabled (`--no-ttr` opts out). Without
ttr, steps run sequentially with Vitest capped at two workers.

## What runs for which paths

| Changed paths | Steps |
| --- | --- |
| Any | Branch name (same pattern as `branch-name-check.yaml`), source-size ceiling, docs inventory and app SEO `--check` |
| JS/TS/JSON/CSS outside `apps/mobile` | Biome `check --error-on-warnings` on those files (pinned 2.5.13); Oxlint on JS/TS files as an **advisory** step |
| `apps/*` or `packages/*` source | App-session, satellite cookie and server-console guards |
| A workspace's source, `tsconfig*.json` or `package.json` | Type-check of the projects its `type-check` script checks |
| A workspace with a Vitest config | Changed tests plus colocated `foo.test.ts(x)` and `__tests__/foo.test.ts(x)` siblings |
| `scripts/`, `.github/actions/`, `plugins/` | Changed and sibling `node --test` files |
| `.github/workflows/` or `.github/actions/` | Workflow concurrency, Bun pin and workflow-config policy tests |
| `apps/mobile/` | `flutter gen-l10n` first when ARB files changed, `dart format` on changed Dart files, then `flutter analyze lib test` exactly as `mobile.yaml` runs it |
| `apps/*/messages/*.json` | i18n sort and en/vi key parity |
| Migrations, docs, web API routes | Migration timestamps, docs audit, legacy route wrappers, mobile API mappings |

Oxlint stays advisory until a scope records Biome parity under the
[Oxc adoption rules](/build/development-tools/oxc-cloudflare-adoption); Biome
remains the blocking formatter and linter. Paused runtimes are excluded.

## Type-checking without built declarations

CI builds `@tuturuuu/types`, `supabase`, `internal-api` and `masonry` before
type-checking. Local checkouts usually lack those `dist` declarations, which
produces thousands of missing-module errors and implicit-`any` cascades. The
gate runs `tsc -p <project> --noEmit --incremental false --composite false` per
project and classifies diagnostics:

- With every workspace declaration present, all diagnostics block.
- When declarations are cold, missing-module errors citing an unbuilt workspace
  package are ignored. Configuration errors (`TS5xxx`/`TS6xxx`, including
  `TS6059`) and errors in changed files that do not import an unbuilt package
  block. Everything else is reported as an advisory count.

Cold mode cannot see fallout in unchanged files (for example consumers of
regenerated database types); the CI type-check remains authoritative.

## Optional pre-push hook

`bun install` already points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`. The pre-push hook
is inert until you opt in:

```bash
git config tuturuuu.prePush true   # every push in this clone and its worktrees
TUTURUUU_PRE_PUSH=1 git push       # a single push
TUTURUUU_PRE_PUSH=0 git push       # skip once while opted in
```

The hook checks committed changes only and skips deletions or pushes of refs
other than `HEAD`. Agents should run `bun check:changed` explicitly before
pushing whether or not the hook is enabled.

## Regression coverage

`scripts/check-changed.test.js`, `scripts/check-changed/plan.test.js`,
`scripts/check-changed/type-check.test.js` and `scripts/ts-diagnostics.test.js`
cover path mapping, the branch pattern's parity with the workflow, hook opt-in,
ttr queueing and cold-declaration classification.
